guarantees.claim: wr_err is asserted when reg_we is 1 and for at least one bit addr_hit[i] (i in 0..58) the expression (|(HMAC_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be)) is true; otherwise wr_err is low.

assumptions.claim: External register write control logic must suppress the write transaction and not update any register when wr_err is asserted.
assumptions.cond: reg_we is high and wr_err becomes high
assumptions.risk: If the write proceeds despite wr_err=1, a write to a prohibited byte lane in a security-sensitive register (e.g., key, digest, configuration lock) may succeed, breaking access control and potentially corrupting or exposing secrets.

assumptions.claim: addr_hit is a one-hot vector; exactly one addr_hit[i] is high for the currently addressed register.
assumptions.cond: during any register access with reg_we=1
assumptions.risk: Multiple simultaneous addr_hit assertions could cause wr_err to be spuriously asserted due to a permission mismatch on a non-accessed register, falsely aborting a valid write.

uncertain_points.claim: The error condition ORs across all addr_hit bits; it is unclear if this is the intended behavior or if the protection should only consider the actual one-hot register. If multiple addr_hit bits are asserted due to a decoder bug, the resulting spurious wr_err may not be handled correctly.
uncertain_points.cond: when addr_hit is not one-hot (e.g., decoder glitch or error)
uncertain_points.risk: A valid access could be mistakenly rejected, potentially causing a denial-of-service or an unexpected bus error within the HMAC IP.
